descriptions.text: In the wee hours of December 19, Youbit was dealt a death blow in the form of another hack. The exchange, which was also hit in April, is closing down in the fallout of the most recent attack. As revealed on its website, they had been forced to terminate its services after suffering another hack. The hackers ran off with 17% of Youbit’s funds, enough to drive the exchange into bankruptcy.

On 19 December 2017, Youbit, a South Korean cryptocurrency exchange, suffered a major compromise of its hot wallet on Bitcoin, resulting in the loss of approximately 17% of its total assets. The incident forced the exchange to shut down operations and file for bankruptcy. The exact loss amount remains undisclosed. Attackers gained access to the private keys of Youbit's hot wallet, allowing them to withdraw a significant portion of the exchange's funds.
